scope: Full daily personal-investment research refresh across the existing Power Stack universe and established themes. No UI, scoring, automation or backend changes.

keyChanges.change: Unitree's Shanghai STAR Market debut materially strengthens evidence of investor appetite for humanoid robotics but weakens the stock-specific risk/reward after the shares closed roughly 460% above the IPO price. Commercial adoption remains much less mature than the valuation signal. Keep the adoption hierarchy unchanged: warehouse/fixed automation, then cobots/mobile manipulation, then industrial humanoids, then general-purpose humanoids. Do not promote Unitree at debut valuation.

keyChanges.theme: AI / Data Centres + Power / Grid + Water / Cooling
keyChanges.change: Texas's data-centre audit is now a cross-stack constraint rather than merely a power issue. The governor's directive explicitly requires projects to disclose grid dependence, on-site generation, water sourcing/reuse and cooling technology. This increases the relative value of integrated power/cooling, closed-loop and water-efficient solutions while increasing execution risk for projects dependent on unverified grid/water assumptions. Existing Vertiv/ECL/MOD/XYL and grid-equipment exposures remain preferred; no new ticker was required.

Brent settled at $91.62 and WTI at $85.83 on August 19 as Hormuz uncertainty persisted. U.S. crude inventories rose 4.4m barrels, but refinery utilisation reached 97.2% and refined-product scarcity remained supportive. Maintain the split thesis: crude is geopolitically supported but demand/inventory-sensitive; refiners remain tactically advantaged by product tightness.

China's reactor buildout remains structurally supportive. Eight additional reactors were approved at the end of July and CGN's Taipingling 2 entered commercial operation on August 3. Existing China nuclear exposures remain supported; no duplicate name promoted.

BHP's FY2026 result continues to validate the copper crossover thesis: copper has overtaken iron ore as its largest earnings contributor. No conviction change one day after promotion; valuation and execution discipline remain the gating issues.

ism.interpretation: The July signal still favours physical bottlenecks: strong production/orders/backlog, customers' inventories that are too low, and persistent shortages in copper, electrical/electronic components, memory and semiconductors. Services demand is expanding but employment contracted and prices accelerated, preserving inflation/rate risk.
ism.rawSubmissionCaveat: No public repository contains ISM's confidential individual survey submissions. Only aggregate diffusion indices and ISM-selected respondent comments are public.

researchGaps: Reassess Texas data-centre project economics after the August 20 PUCT/ERCOT discussion is fully published, particularly which projects can self-supply power and water rather than merely holding interconnection requests.

Build a more granular China/Hong Kong robotics component screen for motion control, reducers, servos, machine vision and sensors; Unitree's debut increases urgency but not the attractiveness of chasing the OEM at debut valuation.
Continue the Malaysia-listed water/cooling screen for a genuinely differentiated Bursa exposure rather than forcing a weak proxy.
Maintain live valuation discipline on high-conviction grid/cooling names as long-end yields remain a material discount-rate risk.
